versions.changelog:
Memoise the File Transformation probe and cover the upgrade path

Follow-up review of the #51 fix.

The availability probe scans every assembly in every load context, and it
ran on each /web request — i.e. on every full page load, under the lock
AssemblyLoadContext.All takes. Latch a positive result instead: plugin
assemblies are never unloaded mid-process, so once File Transformation
has been seen the answer cannot change.

The latch is deliberately positive-only. Caching a negative would risk
pinning noFileTransformation from a probe that ran before its
assembly finished loading, and a stale negative is exactly what makes the
middleware trample other plugins again — the bug being fixed. A stale
positive is not reachable.

Memoising inside IsFileTransformationAvailable rather than in the
middleware also keeps the middleware's test seam honest: tests swap the
delegate wholesale and never touch the latch.

Added tests: the probe must report false when File Transformation is not
loaded (a false positive would make the middleware stand down on servers
that have no File Transformation, leaving the script uninjected), it must
be stable across repeated calls, and the physical-file upgrade path must
not double-inject.

That last one confirms the fallback chain composes: when an older version
has already patched index.html on disk, File Transformation reads the
patched file and runs our callback over it, and InjectScript's
already-present check makes the second pass a no-op.

Also document the full three-step injection chain in ARCHITECTURE.md.
